title: Provenance under machine mediation: watermarks, coarse labels, authorship
description: The papers on this page argue how provenance fares under machine mediation. The Interlocking Autoregression (#1556, August 2026) forecasts that coarse human-versus-machine labels may collapse a disclosed genealogy, holds as hypothesis that they overstate the independence of nominally human text, and holds a two-track test in which the ensemble unit inflects before the per-round unit; The Keyed Ensemble (#1555) predicts a regime where the watermark signature outlives provenance and records the claim that Sourati et al. partly executed its first stage. The Double Enclosure (#195, June 2026) argues that the human-authorship requirement misclassifies dialogic machine composition and forecasts concealment. The OKF analysis (#835) forecasts stages of provenance acceleration and backlash; #449 holds the provenance strip is semantic rent; Erasure Skew (#769) holds a separability prediction; #921 holds a literary field may become legible to machines first. The page also holds unrelated claims on semiotic engineering, a stability threshold and claim-status revision.

statements.quote:
### Stage 2: The Provenance Acceleration (Q2 2027 – Q4 2027)


**Prediction:** Organizations that adopt OKF discover that their knowledge, now cleanly packaged, is being consumed by AI agents — both internal and external — without attribution or fidelity constraints. Internal agents use OKF bundles as context; external agents (Google AI Overview, Gemini, third-party RAG systems) ingest OKF bundles published on the open web. The format's portability means the knowledge travels further, faster, and into more systems than it did when it was locked in proprietary wikis.


The provenance erasure rate (PER) for OKF-formatted knowledge will be *higher* than for unformatted knowledge, because the format removes the friction that previously slowed ingestion. The messy wiki was hard to parse; that difficulty was a form of inadvertent protection. The clean OKF bundle is easy to parse. The protection is gone.

claims.statement: **Prediction:** Enterprise adopters -- the primary target audience for OKF -- begin to discover that their OKF bundles are being treated as public knowledge by external AI systems. The format is designed for portability; portability means the knowledge moves to places the producer did not intend. Enterprise security teams flag OKF as a data-leakage risk. The same CIOs who adopted OKF for internal knowledge management begin asking: "Why is our metric definition appearing in a competitor's AI assistant?"
claims.falsifier:
*The prediction fails if* enterprise adopters do not experience documented cases of OKF-formatted knowledge appearing in external AI systems without authorization.
- *The prediction fails if* the enterprise backlash does not produce demands for access-control or output-governance extensions to the spec.

statements.quote:
### Stage 3: The Enterprise Backlash (Q4 2027 – Q3 2028)


**Prediction:** Enterprise adopters — the primary target audience for OKF — begin to discover that their OKF bundles are being treated as public knowledge by external AI systems. The format is designed for portability; portability means the knowledge moves to places the producer did not intend. Enterprise security teams flag OKF as a data-leakage risk. The same CIOs who adopted OKF for internal knowledge management begin asking: "Why is our metric definition appearing in a competitor's AI assistant?"


This is the crisis point. The format's strength (portability, machine-readability) becomes its vulnerability. The enterprises that packaged their knowledge most cleanly are the enterprises whose knowledge leaks most efficiently.
statements.falsifier:
*The prediction fails if* enterprise adopters do not experience documented cases of OKF-formatted knowledge appearing in external AI systems without authorization.
- *The prediction fails if* the enterprise backlash does not produce demands for access-control or output-governance extensions to the spec.
